---
title: "Metrics for Comparing Tabular Datasets"
description: "Mathematics and code for comparing two same-schema tables through data fidelity, missingness fidelity, utility, and privacy metrics."
author: "Samer El Kababji"
toc: false
---

This series develops metrics for comparing two tabular datasets, $X$ and $Y$,
that share a schema but may contain different values and different numbers of
rows. Neither table is assumed to be real or synthetic.

The introduction separates two views of the tables:

- the original $X,Y$ and their missingness masks $M_X,M_Y$; and
- complete metric-ready representations $\widetilde X,\widetilde Y$ produced
  by one shared transformation.

Later lessons will use these views to develop data-fidelity,
missingness-fidelity, utility, and privacy metrics one at a time.

All notebooks construct the example through the same
[shared Python module](example_data.py), keeping the tables and their derived
views identical across the series.

::: {.lesson-grid}
::: {.lesson-card}
### [1. Generating and Preparing Example Data](1.0-generating-and-preparing-example-data.ipynb)

Construct two small mixed-type tables, expose their missingness masks, and
construct their shared complete representation.

**Prerequisites:** basic Python and introductory data-frame concepts.
:::

::: {.lesson-card}
### [2. Data Fidelity Metric: Correlation-Matrix Difference](2.0-data-fidelity-metric-correlation-matrix-difference.ipynb)

Build the mixed association matrices of $\widetilde X$ and $\widetilde Y$ with
Pearson correlation, $V^2$, and $\eta^2$, then compare them with the Frobenius
norm used by SynthEval 1.6.2.

**Prerequisites:** [1. Generating and Preparing Example Data](1.0-generating-and-preparing-example-data.ipynb).
:::

::: {.lesson-card}
### [3. Data Fidelity Metric: Average Empirical Hellinger Distance](3.0-data-fidelity-metric-average-empirical-hellinger-distance.ipynb)

Align categorical supports and numerical histograms, calculate one Hellinger
distance per column, and average them.
:::

::: {.lesson-card}
### [4. Missingness Fidelity Metric: Marginal Missingness Hellinger Distance](4.0-missingness-fidelity-metric-marginal-missingness-hellinger-distance.ipynb)

Compare the Bernoulli observed/missing distribution of every incomplete
column.
:::

::: {.lesson-card}
### [5. Missingness Fidelity Metric: Joint Missingness Hellinger Distance](5.0-missingness-fidelity-metric-joint-missingness-hellinger-distance.ipynb)

Compare the empirical distribution of complete row-wise missingness patterns.
:::

::: {.lesson-card}
### [6. Missingness Fidelity Metric: Missingness–Value Dependence Gap](6.0-missingness-fidelity-metric-dependence-gap.ipynb)

Use independent-holdout AUROC to test whether $X$ and $Y$ teach the same
missingness–value dependence.
:::

::: {.lesson-card}
### [7. Utility Metric: Independent-Holdout AUROC Difference](7.0-utility-metric-independent-holdout-auroc-difference.ipynb)

Train the same model families on $X$ and $Y$, then score both sides on one
untouched holdout.
:::

::: {.lesson-card}
### [8. Privacy Metric: Exact-Match Rate](8.0-privacy-metric-exact-match-rate.ipynb)

Measure the share of released rows in $Y$ that exactly reproduce a row of $X$.
:::

::: {.lesson-card}
### [9. Privacy Metric: Distance-to-Closest-Record Membership-Inference AUC](9.0-privacy-metric-dcr-membership-inference-auc.ipynb)

Use closest-record distance to distinguish training members from independent
non-members.
:::
:::

## Series roadmap

### Complete metric-ready representations

- **Data fidelity:** correlation-matrix difference and average empirical Hellinger
  distance.
- **Utility:** independent-holdout AUROC difference.
- **Privacy:** exact-match rate and distance-to-closest-record
  membership-inference AUC.

### Original incomplete tables

- **Missingness fidelity:** marginal missingness Hellinger distance, joint
  missingness Hellinger distance, and the missingness–value dependence gap.
